title: kubiq APM Integration Guide
description: Connect Node.js, Python, Java, Go and Next.js applications with tested, authenticated tracing.
endpointNotes: kubiq accepts OTLP HTTP JSON at /api/apm/v1/traces, not direct protobuf. Use the complete backend URL, including its optional prefix. Example production URL: https://priyanshumodi.in/kubiq-api/api/apm/v1/traces. Local development may use http://localhost:3001/api/apm/v1/traces. Use HTTPS for remote ingestion. Set a distinct OTEL_SERVICE_NAME per application. Never expose the ingestion token in browser/client code.

collector.description: Run the pinned Collector beside the application in the same network namespace (same Pod or host). Its receiver binds to loopback; a separate Docker network needs an explicitly private listener and access restriction, not a public port. The Collector forwards JSON with bearer authentication. This Collector is separately installed; kubiq does not automatically provide one.

blocks.title: Collector configuration
blocks.code:
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 127.0.0.1:4318
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 50
    send_batch_max_size: 50
exporters:
  otlphttp/kubiq:
    traces_endpoint: ${env:KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT}
    encoding: json
    compression: none
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer ${env:KUBIQ_INGESTION_TOKEN}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlphttp/kubiq]

blocks.title: Start the Collector in its own environment
blocks.code:
# These variables belong to the Collector process, not the application.
export KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT="https://<kubiq-host><backend-context>/api/apm/v1/traces"
# Supply KUBIQ_INGESTION_TOKEN using your secret manager.
# Download and verify the official otelcol-contrib v0.123.0 binary for your OS.
otelcol-contrib validate --config=collector.yaml
otelcol-contrib --config=collector.yaml

verification: Send real requests to an instrumented HTTP route, then find OTEL_SERVICE_NAME in APM & Traces. Check a trace waterfall and downstream parent/child spans. Allow the batch interval or graceful shutdown to flush. HTTP 401 means ingestion authentication failed; HTTP 415 indicates the wrong wire format; a private Collector must be running before protobuf clients start. An HTTP acceptance response alone is not proof of persisted spans. MongoDB or MySQL APM storage must be enabled; JSON-only storage does not persist APM traces. Log correlation additionally requires log ingestion containing the trace ID. The kubiq backend controlled profile can additionally capture actual MySQL/MariaDB and MongoDB calls with KUBIQ_TRACING_QUERY_DETAILS=true on the server. Its statement/command panel shows bounded query details with passwords, credentials and opaque body/configuration values redacted. Other query values remain visible to APM readers. Generic runtime integrations must explicitly instrument database dependencies; this flag alone does not install database hooks in an arbitrary application.

runtimes.label: Node.js
runtimes.description: Preload the kubiq wrapper before importing HTTP, Express, NestJS or Fastify. It instruments supported installed modules; it does not cover every database or framework automatically.

blocks.title: Install the wrapper
blocks.code: npm install kubiq-apm@1.1.1

blocks.title: Configure private environment
blocks.code:
# Supply the token using your secret manager; never commit it.
export KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT="https://<kubiq-host><backend-context>/api/apm/v1/traces"
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="my-service"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT="$KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS="Authorization=Bearer ${KUBIQ_INGESTION_TOKEN:?Set the ingestion token securely}"

blocks.title: Start your existing application
blocks.code: node --require kubiq-apm/auto app.js

blocks.title: Advanced alternative: manual OpenTelemetry (do not combine with wrapper preload)
blocks.code:
# Use this only instead of kubiq-apm/auto.
npm install @opentelemetry/sdk-node@0.48.0 @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node@0.41.1 @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http@0.48.0
# Configure the same endpoint, service name and authorization header above.
# Create tracing.cjs using the next block, then run:
node --require ./tracing.cjs app.js

blocks.title: Advanced alternative configuration
Opt-in controlled server tracing (instead of auto preload)

runtimes.label: Python
runtimes.description: Run the local Collector first. Bootstrap plugins in the application virtual environment, then start your application with the wrapper. The bundled exporter uses protobuf; changing its protocol string does not make it a JSON exporter.

blocks.title: Install and bootstrap the wrapper
blocks.code:
python -m pip install kubiq-apm==1.0.1
kubiq-apm install

blocks.title: Configure the application environment
blocks.code:
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="my-service"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT="http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="http/protobuf"
export OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER="none"
export OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER="none"
# Do not forward kubiq's ingestion token to this local receiver.

blocks.title: Start your existing application
blocks.code:
# Flask example; install Flask in this virtual environment first.
kubiq-apm flask --app app run --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
# Alternatives:
# kubiq-apm uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
# kubiq-apm python manage.py runserver

runtimes.label: Java
runtimes.description: Download opentelemetry-javaagent v2.14.0 from its official GitHub release and verify its checksum. Start the local Collector first. The existing authenticated Zipkin receiver remains supported for previously configured clients; OTLP through the Collector is the recommended setup.

blocks.title: Download and verify the official Java agent
blocks.code:
curl --fail --location --output opentelemetry-javaagent.jar https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/releases/download/v2.14.0/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar
printf '16f8e28fa1ddcd56ed85bf633bd1d1fbc78ea7c4cc50e8c5726b2a319f5058c8  opentelemetry-javaagent.jar\n' | sha256sum --check

blocks.title: Configure the application environment
blocks.code:
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="my-service"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT="http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="http/protobuf"
export OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER="none"
export OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER="none"
# Do not forward kubiq's ingestion token to this local receiver.

blocks.title: Start your existing Spring Boot jar
blocks.code:
java -javaagent:opentelemetry-javaagent.jar \
  -Dotel.traces.exporter=otlp \
  -jar my-app.jar

runtimes.label: Next.js
runtimes.description: For Next.js 15/16 App Router on the Node runtime, use instrumentation.ts at the project root (or src/). Do not preload kubiq-apm/auto as well: that would initialize tracing twice. Edge/browser instrumentation is not included. Next.js 13/14 requires its legacy experimental.instrumentationHook setting; current versions do not. Set KUBIQ_TRACE_PROPAGATION_ORIGINS to the trusted downstream service origins that should receive trace context; external destinations are not enabled by default.

blocks.title: Install compatible tracing packages
blocks.code: npm install kubiq-apm@1.1.1 @vercel/otel@1.13.0

blocks.title: Configure server-only environment
blocks.code:
# Supply the token using your secret manager; never commit it.
export KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT="https://<kubiq-host><backend-context>/api/apm/v1/traces"
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="my-service"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT="$KUBIQ_TRACES_ENDPOINT"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS="Authorization=Bearer ${KUBIQ_INGESTION_TOKEN:?Set the ingestion token securely}"
# Comma-separated origins of your own trusted downstream services only.
export KUBIQ_TRACE_PROPAGATION_ORIGINS="https://your-internal-api.example.test"

blocks.title: Register tracing before requests
Build and start the Node server
blocks.code:
npm run build
npm run start

runtimes.label: Go
runtimes.description: Unlike the Java agent or Node/Python wrappers, Go needs explicit tracing initialization and HTTP handler/client wrappers. Start the local Collector first.

blocks.title: Install compatible OpenTelemetry modules
blocks.code: go get go.opentelemetry.io/otel@v1.34.0 go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk@v1.34.0 go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp@v1.34.0 go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp@v0.59.0

blocks.title: Configure the application environment
blocks.code:
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="my-service"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT="http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="http/protobuf"
export OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER="none"
export OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER="none"
# Do not forward kubiq's ingestion token to this local receiver.

blocks.title: Initialize tracing and instrument HTTP
Start your application
blocks.code: go run .

shellNotes: Commands use POSIX shell syntax. In PowerShell, set environment variables with $env:NAME = "value", then start the application in that same environment. The ingestion token must come from your secret manager, never client-side code.
